review_method: Direct assistant review of all 95 complete supplied table records, including all parts, body rows, context and notes; no OCR, external model calls, or assignment/schema edits.

candidates.label: commodity geography
candidates.definition: Geographic origins and regional distribution of products or productive resources across several economic sectors.
includes: Inventories pairing many commodities with their producing regions.
Mixed crop, animal-product, mineral, timber and manufactured-product origin lists.
excludes: A single commodity adequately described by its commodity tag.
Quantitative multi-domain economic barometers, which use economic-indicators.
Trade quantities by origin or destination without a substantive inventory of regional products.
candidates.why_existing_tags_do_not_fit: The tables span agriculture, mining, forestry and manufactured goods without output measures. crop-production, mineral-production and industrial-output are sector-specific; economic-indicators explicitly concerns indicator summaries. Picking three incidental commodities would misrepresent the inventory.

candidates.label: route distances
candidates.definition: Travel distances between named places, ports or route stages, including origin-destination mileage lists and distance matrices.
includes: Sea, coastal, river and overland distance matrices.
Direct and via-route mileage comparisons between named endpoints.
excludes: Total network length or newly constructed mileage without endpoint-distance comparisons.
Fares and freight charges, which use freight-and-transport-costs.
Physical river length without a travel-route subject.
candidates.why_existing_tags_do_not_fit: shipping and inland-navigation already cover many mode-specific examples and should not be withheld. The residual gap is a single cross-mode discovery term for the distance reference itself, especially the Siberian tables where a transport mode is not explicitly stated. This is an optional useful facet, not evidence that every distance table needs a new term before it can receive any detail.

candidates.label: printing
candidates.definition: The printing industry and the establishments, equipment and production processes used to produce printed matter.
includes: Commercial and mission printing establishments and presses.
Printing, typesetting, lithography and related print-production activity.
excludes: Paper and pulp production without printing.
Publication-title or circulation statistics alone, which use books, newspapers or periodicals.
candidates.why_existing_tags_do_not_fit: The list is of printing works across newspaper and mission presses, rather than one publication format. books, newspapers and periodicals cannot represent the print-production industry collectively; paper-and-pulp describes a different production stage.

candidates.label: demobilisation
candidates.definition: Disbanding armed units or releasing personnel from military service, including the administrative and financial arrangements for doing so.
includes: Demobilisation numbers, discharge arrangements and unit reductions.
excludes: Recruitment or conscription into service.
Routine peacetime unit organisation without a release or disbandment subject.
Welfare of former servicemen after discharge without a substantive demobilisation process.
candidates.why_existing_tags_do_not_fit: army and public-budgets can already cover the troop-disbandment expenditure. recruitment-and-conscription is the opposite process; war-and-mobilisation does not explicitly distinguish release or reduction. The proposed term supplies useful process specificity rather than curing a total lack of existing tags.

candidates.label: professional associations
candidates.definition: Organised bodies representing or coordinating members of a learned or licensed profession and their governance, membership or professional activities.
includes: Medical, legal, engineering and similar professional associations.
Professional association committees, officers and membership.
excludes: Commercial chambers and industry associations, which use business-associations.
Worker bargaining organisations, which use trade-unions.
A roster of licensed practitioners without an association, or an institution devoted solely to scientific research.
candidates.why_existing_tags_do_not_fit: The National Medical Association roster concerns professional self-organisation. medical-services concerns provision and use of care; business-associations concerns commercial or industrial representation; scientific-research requires a substantive research organisation or activity. None specifically represents this professional body.

candidates.label: mercury
candidates.definition: Mercury (quicksilver), its ores and metal, as a mineral resource, extracted product or traded commodity.
includes: Quicksilver deposits, output and commodity imports or exports.
excludes: Mercury merely mentioned as an incidental ingredient in a pharmaceutical or chemical inventory.
Mixed mineral production without a substantive mercury component.
candidates.why_existing_tags_do_not_fit: exports and mineral-production already fit this mixed export/output table. A mercury term would add the same commodity precision already provided for tin, antimony and tungsten. It should be considered with evidence from the other review batches, not added simply because this table currently has no tags.

candidates.label: holidays and commemorations
candidates.definition: Recognised public holidays and recurring civic or historical commemoration days and the occasions they mark.
includes: Official public holiday and anniversary calendars.
Dates and events commemorated by state or civic observances.
excludes: General historical event chronologies.
Calendar conversion, era equivalences and time standards without an observance subject.
Astronomical events without a holiday or commemoration.
candidates.why_existing_tags_do_not_fit: calendars-and-time is a reasonable existing broad reference tag, but its current definition emphasises systems for reckoning dates rather than the occasions observed. Either add this specific cultural subject or explicitly extend the existing definition; do not create both a public-holidays and a separate commemorations term.

candidates.label: colonies and leased territories
candidates.definition: Colonial possessions and formally leased territories as political holdings, including inventories of their status and administering powers.
includes: Lists of foreign possessions grouped by holding power.
Comparisons of colonies and leased territories as geopolitical units.
excludes: Ordinary production or population statistics merely published in a colony.
Urban concession systems in a nominally sovereign state, which use foreign-concessions.
Annexation or protectorate establishment and termination, when annexation-and-protectorates is the precise subject.
candidates.why_existing_tags_do_not_fit: This possession list mixes colonies, leased territories and formerly German holdings. foreign-concessions is deliberately narrower than all colonies, colonial-administration concerns governing machinery, and annexation-and-protectorates concerns changes or terms of status. A political-holdings inventory is not cleanly represented by those definitions. This proposed tag must never become a default for all tables from colonial volumes.

existing_tag_fits.explanation: The table lists proposed government loans secured on land tax, stamp revenue and public bonds. public-debt explicitly includes government loans; an unidentified lender does not require a foreign-loans tag.

The table quantifies the consequences of depreciated subsidiary coinage for a named tramway system. Currency and tramway operating results are both substantive; no separate conversion-losses tag is necessary.

The body lists named main highways and their routes, with some mileages. It is road infrastructure described by itinerary rather than a road-traffic table. Existing roads-and-bridges is suitable; an itinerary-specific subject tag is not required.
Postal employees are substantially classified by nationality. Rules permit nationality-and-ethnicity as a shared detail without automatically adding population as a high-level topic.

The named chancellor, vice-chancellors, deans and registrar are the administration of a specific university. higher-education covers universities, so a special university-governance tag is not required.

river-conservancy explicitly includes conservancy boards and administration, and government-offices covers official staffing. The table also has a substantive count of 13 Chinese engineers and surveyors.

A reference calendar of annually recurring public holidays can use the existing broad date-reckoning tag. The definition should explicitly confirm observance calendars if a separate holidays-and-commemorations subject is not adopted.

Mercury export tonnages and concentrate output already support exports and the aggregate mineral-production tag. A mercury term would improve commodity precision, not rescue otherwise unclassifiable data.

classification_notes.note: The gift table has explicit item quantities and a 60-ounce object weight; its text-tables flag conflicts with the same list in other editions. Treat this as a future flag-QA issue, not a vocabulary change.
First trade-contact years are dates in an event list. The statistical/text distinction should be harmonised with the other editions, where this is flagged textual.
The road itinerary contains explicit measured mileages; the conservancy staff table contains 13 engineers/surveyors. Their existing text flags deserve later checking. No flags were altered.

recommendation: Prioritise commodity-geography, printing and professional-associations. Consider demobilisation and route-distances as useful refinements; assess mercury, holiday and colonial-territory terms against the other review batches. Most blanks in this batch are over-restrictive applications of existing tags.
